This page shows how to register the input-provenance, curation, and packaging
notebooks in the project-root target script. The graph itself is declared, with
its explanatory narrative, in those notebooks. Scientific execution is a
separate, explicit container-runtime operation.

::: {.manual-prereq title="Confirm The Input Boundary"}

Confirm that `stagecoach_manifest.yml` exists at the repository root and that
`data/inputs/` contains the staged files required by the Curation page.

:::

## Register the notebook graph

In the repository-root `_targets.R` created by `targets::use_targets()`, replace
its example targets with the following pipeline list. Only notebooks containing
target declarations are registered.

```r
library(targets)
library(tarchetypes)

list(
  tarchetypes::tar_tangle("notebooks/pipeline/16_page-stage-inputs.qmd"),
  tarchetypes::tar_tangle("notebooks/pipeline/18_page-targets-curation.qmd"),
  tarchetypes::tar_tangle("notebooks/pipeline/19_page-package-release.qmd")
)
```

`_targets.R` is deliberately maintained at the project root, alongside the
other project-level configuration. It is the single entry point that
`targets::tar_make()` reads; the `pipeline/` directory holds notebooks, not a
second targets project.

```sh
# From an adequate allocation, execute the root-level graph in the container.
scripts/kiribati-biomarkers Rscript scripts/run-pipeline.R
```

The command is intentionally not a Quarto render hook. It fails if the
scientific pipeline fails, and it runs with the container's Spack R runtime and
project-local package library rather than the host environment.
